Model vol = √(β² × SPX implied² + realised idiosyncratic vol²). Premium = implied − model: positive is rich to the model, negative is cheap. Click a row to mark the name on the matrix and scatter. Click a header to sort.
Data as of the latest market close. For informational purposes only. Basket = the 100 largest S&P 500 members by today's market cap, weights fixed and renormalised over the names with data (at least 80). Fair vol = √(w′·S·C·S·w): S is each member's ex-earnings ATM implied vol at the tenor, C the realised pairwise correlation of ex-earnings daily log returns over the tenor's window (1M 21d, 3M 63d, 6M 126d, 12M 252d). 100 names diversify less than 500, so the basket's realised vol runs above the index's; adjusted fair vol scales fair vol by index realised ÷ basket realised over the same window, and the spread is SPX implied minus adjusted fair. Implied correlation is the single average correlation that reprices SPX implied (on the same basis) from the members' implieds. Sector implied correlation comes from each sector ETF's implied against its basket members (sectors need 3+ names; the rest sit in the cross-sector block), and cross-sector implied correlation is solved so the block matrix reprices SPX. The implied matrix shifts each realised pair by its block's implied-minus-realised average, clipped to ±100.
